scope: Orléans 2014 dlp base game, 2–4 players; English booklet pp.12–21, base Place Tiles pp.22–23, components p.24. Excludes optional Place Tile exclusion and expansions.

questions.question: In a 3-player Census, two players tie furthest ahead and one is alone furthest behind. Who gains or pays? What changes for an unequal 2-player Census?
Your Knight draw allowance is 6, but only two Market spaces are free. Must you draw six? May you draw more than two? What happens to unused Market Followers?
May you partially fill an action over several rounds, execute it before it is full, or save a fully activated action for a later round? Where do its Followers go when it is eventually executed?
How do players alternate actions in Phase 5? If you pass with an unused activated action, can you act again later this round and what happens to that activation?
What does the Farm House action recruit, where does it go, and what track movement and immediate reward follow?
What three professions can Village recruit, and what distinct track reward accompanies each?
You just recruited a Craftsman. Can its Technology help another action this Action Phase? What must your first Technology replace, and what are the placement limits for all Technology?
On your first Trader-track advance may you choose a category II Place? What categories are allowed later, and may players inspect the stacks?
What do University, Castle and Monastery each give and where do recruits go? Does the fourth Knight increase the draw allowance, and what happens once a character track is at its last space?
Can a Monk replace a Knight for an ordinary action? Can a Knight or Technology replace a required Monk? Can a Monk replace a required profession on Beneficial Deeds?
What exactly does one Ship or Wagon action move, and how many goods can you take if two lie on that connection? May you use an empty connection?
What does Guildhall build, where must your Merchant be, and may you build where an opponent has already built? State the Orléans exception.
What does Scriptorium do? When Development movement lands on or passes coin, Citizen and status spaces, what rewards/status changes occur?

Can Town Hall work with one Follower, can it send two in one action, and can your starting colored Followers be used? What rewards and destinations apply, including Canalization and completing a Deed?
What does Pilgrimage forbid, when does it apply, and when are the other events resolved? Which event opens the game?
During Harvest you have wool, wine and coins. Which goods qualify, where does paid food go, and what if you have no food and fewer than five coins?

During Plague you draw a neutral Scholar; during another Plague you draw your colored starting Trader. What is lost, where does it go, do tracks fall, and is a replacement draw required for the starting Trader?
You owe three coins but have only one. Explain torture payment choices, restrictions on sacrificing Followers or Development Points, and where lost items go.
What happens if an action would give an unavailable Character, Technology or Goods Tile? Can it resume when stock returns? What if the coin supply is temporarily empty?

At game end two players tie for most built Trading Stations. Who takes the bonus Citizen? Give final values of all five goods and the scoring formula for stations/Citizens; how are equal final scores broken?
At setup, where are the four starting Followers, Merchant, seven markers, unbuilt Trading Stations and coins placed; what do you receive personally, and who starts?
How are Citizens, Technology, neutral Followers, Place Tile stacks, and map/remaining goods set up in a 4-player game?
Specify the neutral Follower and random Goods removals and the empty map goods-space labels for both 3-player and 2-player setup. What happens to unused colored starting Followers?
Before substitutions or Technology, list the required Followers for Farm House, Village, University, Castle and Monastery.
Before substitutions or Technology, list the required Followers for Ship, Wagon and Guildhall.
Before substitutions or Technology, what Followers activate Scriptorium, and what professions are allowed in Town Hall?
In Phase 3 your allowance is six. May you decline two draws to recover two Followers assigned to actions? Where do they go, and may you instead move them directly between Action Spaces?
May you look into your Followers Bag during play to check its contents? What must you do afterward?
List the seven round phases in order. How does Start Player change, and how is order handled if simultaneous Planning or payments require a sequence? Where do paid and received coins go?
The 18th Hour Glass tile has just been revealed. Do you score immediately, or what part of play remains?
One player has more Farmer tiles in their bag, but a different player is uniquely ahead on the Farmers Track. Who gains the Census coin?
How much does Income pay and what current value determines it?
You have eight goods at Taxes. How much must you pay, do goods types change that calculation, and what happens if you lack the coins?
At Trading Day you have four built stations and six unbuilt in reserve. How much do you receive?

For each of Hayrick, Cheese Factory, Winery, Wool Manufacturer and Tailor Shop, give the printed activation cost, produced good, its source, and whether you may use it when that good is unavailable there.
Give the printed activation cost and reward for Shipping Line, Brewery, Windmill and Library.
Which Follower can activate Pharmacy, what is the legal coin-spending range, and how far does it advance you if you pay two? May you use its effect for zero or four coins?
Give the printed activation cost and coin reward for Cellar, Office and Hospital. What quantity sets each variable payout?
What activates Horse Wagon, what route and distance does it travel, and what does it collect?
What activates Laboratory and what does it give? Could your first ever Technology be placed on Laboratory itself, and could a later one be placed there if no Technology is already on it?
What activates Bathhouse? Describe its normal draw-three procedure, when and where the chosen tiles go, the forbidden destination, and where all other involved Followers go.
Bathhouse draws three Followers, but only one can legally be placed on any allowed Action Space. What may you place and where do the others and the activating Follower go? What if none can be placed?

During the Action Phase, Bathhouse immediately supplies the last needed Follower to another Place. Must that newly activated Place wait for next round, or may you execute it on a later action turn this round if you have not passed?
What activates Sacristy, when is its protection used, which events can it protect against, and where does its Monk go?
Does an activated Sacristy let you recruit a Monk during a Pilgrimage round? Explain the timing.
What does Herb Garden allow Boatmen to replace, and does it permit replacing Knights, Scholars or Monks?
What does School allow Scholars to replace, does School require activation, and may a Scholar replace a required Monk?
With Herb Garden or School, can a substituted Boatman or Scholar fill a differently depicted Beneficial Deed space? Does using Gunpowder Tower instead of Town Hall change that?
Describe Gunpowder Tower: how much capacity it adds, when Followers enter it, the two ways to use them, whether two can go to Deeds in one action, and whether colored starting Followers can be sent.
In a 3-player Census there is one unique leader and two players tied furthest behind. Who gains and who pays?

At the end of round 18, one player has strictly more built Trading Stations than every other player. Who receives the remaining Citizen Tile, when is it awarded, and does it count in final Citizen scoring?
How do you prepare the Hour Glass stack at setup, and who reveals which tile in Phase 1?
How many victory points does each remaining coin score at the end of the game?
Before any track advancement, what are your initial Development Status and Knight-track draw allowance?
After torture, which lost asset type can be regained, and do surrendered goods, Followers, stations, Places or Technology return to their supplies?
